key_insight: QOC-Workbench uses an LLM as an autonomous quantum co-scientist to design and validate cross-paradigm control protocols that go beyond fixed-form numerical optimization.
engineering_relevance: The workflow can help translate quantum control ideas into hardware-compliant schedules, catalysts, and control paths for practical quantum annealing, adiabatic computing, and state engineering.
method: Parses physics literature to propose structural hypotheses for quantum optimal control.
Writes and runs simulation code to test candidate controls directly.
Accumulates reusable control motifs and, for larger systems, switches to an amortized GNN generator for transferable coefficient paths.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful demonstrations on three settings, with autonomous discovery of improved controls in two cases and transfer to larger unseen systems in the third.
watch_item: Because the workflow depends on LLM-generated hypotheses and simulation validation, robustness, reproducibility, and error detection are critical before experimental deployment.
paper_title: LLM-Driven Cross-Paradigm Design for Quantum Optimal Control
